answer: Each epoch the protocol posts seed S and F, first-seen submits already included. A new key lands only if the cipher of (key, S) falls inside 1/(1+F) of the hash space; miss and the submit is dropped. One joiner always fits. After nine, the tenth fits with chance 1/10, so ten live keys cost 55 tries (triangle n(n+1)/2). S is this epoch's beacon: a fresh key cannot reset, split, or pre-age it, and each key gets one hash. A karst spring feeds one lagoon whose mouth shrinks as each hull ties up, so the next boat needs a tighter gap than the last.
